clue.text: A revolutionary device for the traveller

definitions.text: A revolutionary device for the traveller

parts.words: A revolutionary device for the traveller
parts.note: revolutionary suggests politics, but it means a thing that turns round and round, carrying people along the road

explanation.definitionFit: A wheel turns on its axle and is the basic part that moves any cart or car forward.

clue.text: See the boss before ten in this workplace

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud, as on a shield
ten written as figures is 1 and 0, read as the letters I and O

explanation.surface: An instruction to visit the manager before ten o'clock at the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' is not the manager but a stud; 'ten' is the figures 1 0 taken as letters IO.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's or broadcaster's place of work is called a studio.

clue.text: Guarded but fed-up, drew to a close

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word fed is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written
something that drew to a close finished, or ended

explanation.surface: Someone protected yet sick of it all, bringing matters to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FED into DEF; 'fed-up' looks like one word meaning annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: To have guarded something is to have protected it from attack.

clue.text: Coastal disease-nasty

indicators.note: nasty suggests the letters of disease are in a bad, mangled state

explanation.surface: A warning about an unpleasant illness picked up by the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Coastal places lie by the shore, so a seaside town is a coastal one.

clue.text: Just a few words could mean prison!

explanation.surface: A remark that a short statement might land someone in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical unit of a few words, and also the term of punishment a judge passes.

clue.text: A rival proposal read first

indicators.note: first places the piece meaning read ahead of the proposal piece

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or read carefully
a tender is a formal offer or proposal to do a job

explanation.surface: A competitor's bid that was studied before any other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is the charade's order signal; 'read' in the old sense of study is the less familiar meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A contender competes for a prize, so is a rival to the others.

clue.text: Broke, as the trade's bad

indicators.note: bad tells us the letters are in a poor, jumbled order

parts.note: taken as written
the letters of trade's, with its S kept

explanation.surface: A merchant says business is so poor that they are penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges THE TRADES. 'Broke' looks like penniless but means smashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that broke has been smashed into pieces.

clue.text: The woman with no backing gets the bird

parts.note: her refers to a woman

indicators.note: with no backing means the word no is read backwards here

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An unsupported woman ends up being rudely dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns NO into ON. 'gets the bird' sounds like being booed.
explanation.definitionFit: A heron is a long-legged wading bird.

clue.text: Name the time

explanation.surface: A request to state the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: A term is a word naming something, and also a set period such as a school session.

clue.text: Wanting capital

parts.note: reads as short of money, but capital here is the top part, so this means lacking a head

explanation.definitionFit: Capital comes from the Latin for head, so lacking a capital means having no head at all.

clue.text: Property among the finest-a term used by developers

indicators.note: among says the letters lie within the run of words finest-a term

explanation.surface: A remark that a word builders favour is one of the best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' tells us to look inside 'finest-a term'; 'used by developers' nods to housing estates.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is land or possessions owned by someone.

clue.text: Many people of mature years are unfriendly

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword many
the old are people of advanced age

explanation.surface: A claim that most elderly folk are hostile.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold manner is distant and lacks warmth toward others.

clue.text: A mind not perhaps fitted for ruling

indicators.note: perhaps fitted together tells us the letters of a mind not are assembled anew

explanation.surface: A remark that someone's intellect may not suit governing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dominant power holds sway, the controlling one in charge.

clue.text: Most agree to organise a fuel store

indicators.note: organise asks for the letters of most agree to be arranged in a new order

explanation.surface: Most people consent to set up a depot for fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas holder was a large tank for storing town gas.

clue.text: Force the taking of legal action about a rogue

indicators.note: about means the lawsuit word goes around the rogue

parts.note: a case is a lawsuit
a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: Someone compelled to sue a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. 'Force' is a northern English word for a waterfall, not compulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: In the north of England a force is a waterfall, and a cascade is falling water.

clue.text: To show up repeatedly would bring reproval

indicators.note: repeatedly says the word for show up appears twice in a row

parts.note: to come is to show up or arrive

explanation.surface: Turning up again and again would earn a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled exclamation is a mild rebuke, like tut-tut.

clue.text: Went in and made a record

explanation.surface: Someone stepped inside and logged it.
explanation.definitionFit: Passed through a door, and also wrote details into a register or log.

clue.text: Changing a lot in an inhabitant

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of a lot in an are altered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A resident who keeps moving things about.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen or resident of a particular country.

clue.text: Overlooks nothing concerning a blight on the landscape

parts.note: to eye is to look at, so overlooks gives eyes
O is zero, nothing
re is Latin-derived for about or concerning

explanation.surface: A view that ignores nothing about an ugly feature of the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overlooks' seems to mean ignores but here means looks over, watches.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugly building spoiling a view is called an unsightly blot.

clue.text: Standard set by an associate in the ordinary way

parts.note: a norm is a usual standard
an ally is a partner or associate

explanation.surface: A benchmark laid down by a colleague in the usual manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things as usual is behaving in the common, regular manner.

clue.text: A woman of fifty — one-and-fifty before the end of January

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
I is the Roman numeral for one
L again, the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: the end of January means its final letter

explanation.surface: A woman of fifty, one of fifty-one, before the end of January.
explanation.walkthrough: The ages are Roman numerals L, I, L; 'the end of' January gives Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Lily is a girl's given name.

clue.text: Gin can make some reflective

indicators.note: reflective suggests a mirror image, so the word for some is read backwards

parts.note: part means some, a portion

explanation.surface: A gin might make some drinkers thoughtful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflective' turns PART back to front. 'Gin' is not the drink but a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is an old word for a snare used to catch animals.

clue.text: Substitute having some effect

explanation.surface: A stand-in making some impact.
explanation.definitionFit: Serving temporarily in another's post, and also working or operating on something.

clue.text: Turning in of leaves in a plant

indicators.note: turning tells us to read the run of letters from right to left
in says the letters are found inside the words leaves in a

explanation.surface: Foliage curling inward on a garden specimen.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'leaves in a' backwards (A NI SEVAEL) and the plant sits at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Anise is a herb grown for its liquorice-flavoured seeds.

clue.text: Writer in the lead? No, quite the opposite

definitions.text: Writer in the lead? No, quite the opposite

parts.words: Writer in the lead? No, quite the opposite
parts.note: rather than an author leading the field, this is a writing tool with graphite lead held inside it

explanation.definitionFit: A pencil is a writing implement with graphite lead in its core.

clue.text: Seeing a drug cutting pain

indicators.note: cutting means the drug word cuts into the pain word

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Noticing someone use a narcotic to dull an ache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' signals the drug going inside the pain word; 'Seeing' means noticing.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotting something is catching sight of it.

clue.text: Army men writing about a requirement for lots of paper

indicators.note: about means the soldiers and writing go around the letter a

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Soldiers drafting something that needs plenty of stationery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the soldiers and writing wrapping the A; RE (Royal Engineers) is a common army abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is a large bundle of sheets, so reams are a great quantity.

clue.text: The power of sergeants wrongly exercised

indicators.note: wrongly exercised suggests the letters of sergeants are drilled out of order

explanation.surface: NCOs abusing their authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Greatness means eminence, might or importance.
